records.title: [Feature]: Add safe Kanban workspace rebinding after Project primary changes
records.body:
### Problem or Use Case

When a Project primary repository or board default_workdir is corrected after Kanban cards have been created, existing cards retain their materialized workspace_path. The cards continue targeting the old anchor even though `hermes project show` reports the corrected primary.

Observed on Windows 11 with Hermes v0.20.5:

1. A Project was initially created with a wrapper folder as primary; the actual Git repository was one level below it.
2. 2. Nineteen project-linked implementation cards materialized under `<wrapper>/.worktrees/<task-id>`.
3. 3. `hermes project set-primary` corrected the Project to the actual repository.
4. 4. Existing cards kept the old paths.
5. 5. Dispatch rejected them as outside a Git repository and consumed retries until the circuit breaker blocked the cards.
Recovery required recreating every affected card, rewiring dependencies, commenting and archiving the originals, and separately preserving partial worker output. This is error-prone and gives up stable task IDs.

Related work #92645, #92519, and #70865 guards new unanchored or unresolvable cards, but does not repair existing materialized cards after an intentional Project or board-anchor correction. #81336 handles missing worktrees; #91169/#91191 handles reciprocal Project-board binding. Those are adjacent but distinct.

### Proposed Solution

Add a first-class, fail-closed rebind workflow for Project-derived Kanban workspaces.

Suggested shape:

- `hermes project set-primary <project> <path>` and `hermes kanban boards set-default-workdir` should detect active cards whose stored workspace_path was derived from the previous anchor and print an explicit affected-card count.
- - Provide a dry-run/apply repair command, for example `hermes kanban rebind-workspaces --project <project> --from <old-root> --to <new-root> [--apply]`.
- - - Preserve task IDs, bodies, comments, runs, dependency edges, branches, retries, and review state; update only the workspace routing fields and append an auditable event.
- - - - Refuse running/claimed tasks, ambiguous paths, explicit user overrides, branch collisions, and destinations that are not verified Git roots/worktree targets.
- - - - - Distinguish Project-derived paths from explicit workspace overrides, ideally with persisted provenance for newly created tasks.
- - - - - - Verify every rewritten destination before committing the transaction and report exact changed/skipped/refused counts.
- - - - - - - Document that card workspace paths are snapshots at creation time and that changing a Project or board anchor does not silently mutate existing cards.
This should complement, not duplicate, the creation-time validation in the related PRs.

### Alternatives Considered

- Manual recreate/link/unlink/archive preserves audit history but is too complex for bulk recovery and changes task IDs.
- - Re-deriving every workspace dynamically at dispatch would make Project changes unexpectedly mutate active tasks and could redirect explicit overrides.
- - - Creation-time validation alone prevents some future incidents but cannot recover legacy or already-materialized rows.
A scoped, provenance-aware, dry-run-first rebind command is safer and more predictable.

### Feature Type

CLI improvement

### Scope

None

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

records.title: Gradle migration follow-ups (post-#326)
records.body:
PR #326 migrated the build from Ant to Gradle with output verified byte-identical. To keep that PR reviewable and parity-checkable, several improvements were deliberately deferred. This issue tracks them. Parent: #52.

### Build tooling
- [ ] **Try Gradle 9.** The wrapper ships on 8.14.1. Confirm the build runs clean under Gradle 9 and bump when it does. One known item to clear first: a `Task.project`-at-execution-time deprecation in `verifyDistributionPlacement` that Gradle 9 warns on and Gradle 10 removes. _(raised by @jbeckers in #326)_
- [ ] **Consider the Kotlin DSL for the build scripts.** Currently Groovy; Kotlin is Gradle's official recommendation. _(raised in #326, agreed as a follow-up)_
- [ ] **Clean up stale `.gitignore` headers.** ~111 inert commented section headers (`# /client/src/com/...`) date to the original 2017 `.gitignore` and still reference the pre-move layout. Update to `src/main/java` or drop them. _(raised by @jbeckers in #326)_

### Dependencies
- [ ] **Align multi-artifact dependency families with BOMs.** The catalog versions every artifact of a family independently, so a bot can bump part of a set and leave it incoherent with nothing to catch it. That is #389: `log4j-api` stayed at 2.25.3 while `log4j-core` and `log4j-1.2-api` moved to 2.25.4, and the server would not boot. Import `platform(libs.<x>.bom)` for log4j, jackson, netty, jetty, and the AWS SDK. Constrains versions only, pulls nothing transitively, flat explicit list stays intact.
- [ ] **Normalize to transitive resolution, one library at a time.** The migration intentionally pins a non-transitive, audited set matching the historical vendored jars. Enable transitivity per library during routine version bumps, diff against the flat list, reconcile, re-verify with the parity harness. Flat lists remain better for scanning accuracy, so this is a slow bridge with no deadline. _(objection from @jbeckers in the comments)_
- [ ] **CVE burn-down.** An initial dependency-check baseline flagged ~54 distinct CVEs across ~46 jars. Start with the one-line, parity-checkable bumps (netty, jackson-databind, pdfbox), then the harder ones: Jetty 9.4.57 (EOL line), MyBatis (#320), Derby, iText -> OpenPDF (#289), commons-httpclient -> httpclient5. See also #304.
- [ ] **Adopt byte-identical repackaged jars from Maven Central.** 13 vendored jars are content-identical to Central artifacts (the HAPI 2.3 set, jtds, sqlite-jdbc, rsyntaxtextarea, autocomplete) and can be sourced from Central. The 3 genuine forks (javaparser 1.0.8, zip4j 1.3.3, not-going-to-be-commons-ssl) stay vendored.

records.title: `WITH RECURSIVE` based iteration
records.body:
At my shop we do lot of *ELT* where the *T* happens in database.
A typical use case is the following:
- We get JSON files and we insert them inside the database, this is our *E* and *L*
- We write materialized views/queries to process those JSON files, this is our *T*

This has the benefit that everything happens in database, and if there is an error in the business logic we only need to refresh the materialized views. We love materialized views. Our *E* are literally scripts which do a single request and a single INSERT query. And when we need to dump the database, the only content are the JSON files content + definition, so our dumps are very light.

In our context some times we need iteration, for example, we have a feed of events, a single JSON document, we need to process those events accumulating some state, to process the message T[n], we need the state derived from T[1],...,T[n-1]. 
In functional programming languages this is called a `fold`.

In postgres we use `WITH-RECURSIVE` queries, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/14/queries-with.html#QUERIES-WITH-RECURSIVE
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE t(n) AS (
    VALUES (1)
  UNION ALL
    SELECT n+1 FROM t WHERE n < 100
)
SELECT sum(n) FROM t;
```

I can see a world where I would write the body of materialized views in `PRQL`.

pibo data migrate sessions-to-v2 leaves room_id stale on newer re-import
records.body:
## Summary

When `pibo data migrate sessions-to-v2` re-imports a newer legacy session, it updates `metadata_json.chatRoomId` but leaves the structured `sessions.room_id` column at its previous value. The command reports the row as updated and advances `updated_at`, so later migration runs skip the row and preserve the contradiction.

This leaves one Pibo Session associated with two rooms in the same target row. Normal session and Chat data paths use the structured `room_id`, while metadata inspection reports the newer room.

## Base and environment

- Repository: `Pascapone/pibo`
- Base branch: current `upstream/dev`
- Base SHA: `2aef244301f5d181624662fdad53e18e83e80bd9`
- Isolated Docker dev worker with a disposable legacy database and target Pibo home
- No gateway, controller service, provider, or Pibo2 environment was invoked

## Native discovery

I followed the CLI's discovery path before creating the fixture:

```text
pibo data --help
pibo debug --help
pibo debug db --help
pibo debug pty --help
```

The data help describes `migrate sessions-to-v2` as an idempotent import into `pibo.sqlite`; the debug commands provide the native read-only checks below.

## Deterministic fixture

Create a disposable legacy store containing one session assigned to `room_old`:

```js
import { mkdirSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";

const root = "/workspace/.bughunt-fixture/migration-home";
rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });

const db = new DatabaseSync(`${root}/pibo-sessions.sqlite`);
db.exec(`
  CREATE TABLE pibo_sessions (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    pi_session_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    channel TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    profile TEXT NOT NULL,
    owner_scope TEXT,
    parent_id TEXT,
    origin_id TEXT,
    workspace TEXT,
    title TEXT,
    metadata_json TEXT,
    active_model_json TEXT,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
  );
`);
db.prepare("INSERT INTO pibo_sessions VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)").run(
  "ps_room_move_fixture",
  "pi_room_move_fixture",
  "pibo.chat-web",
  "chat",
  "base",
  "shared:app",
  null,
  null,
  "/workspace",
  "Room move fixture",
  JSON.stringify({ chatRoomId: "room_old" }),
  null,
  "2026-08-30T00:00:00.000Z",
  "2026-08-30T00:01:00.000Z",
);
db.close();
```

Run the first import:

```bash
PIBO_HOME=/workspace/.bughunt-fixture/migration-home \
  npm run --silent dev -- data migrate sessions-to-v2 --json
```

It reports `inserted: 1`. A native debug query confirms that both representations initially agree:

```bash
PIBO_HOME=/workspace/.bughunt-fixture/migration-home \
  npm run --silent dev -- debug db query sessions \
  "SELECT id, room_id, metadata_json, updated_at FROM sessions WHERE id = 'ps_room_move_fixture'" \
  --json
```

```json
{
  "id": "ps_room_move_fixture",
  "room_id": "room_old",
  "metadata_json": "{\"chatRoomId\":\"room_old\"}",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-30T00:01:00.000Z"
}
```

Advance the legacy source to a newer room assignment:

```js
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";

const db = new DatabaseSync("/workspace/.bughunt-fixture/migration-home/pibo-sessions.sqlite");
db.prepare("UPDATE pibo_sessions SET metadata_json = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?").run(
  JSON.stringify({ chatRoomId: "room_new" }),
  "2026-08-30T00:02:00.000Z",
  "ps_room_move_fixture",
);
db.close();
```

Run the second import under a real PTY:

```bash
pibo debug pty run \
  --docker-worker pibo-dev-bughunt-functional-20260830-next \
  --workdir /workspace \
  --rows 24 --cols 110 \
  --timeout-ms 15000 --idle-timeout-ms 5000 \
  --artifact-dir /root/code/pibo/.worktrees/bughunt-functional-20260830-next/.bughunt-fixture/pty-second-migration \
  --artifact \
  --expect '"updated": 1' \
  -- env PIBO_HOME=/workspace/.bughunt-fixture/migration-home \
    npm run --silent dev -- data migrate sessions-to-v2 --json
```

## Actual result

The PTY run succeeds and the migration reports a complete update:

```json
{
  "inputExists": true,
  "read": 1,
  "inserted": 0,
  "updated": 1,
  "skipped": 0
}
```

PTY metadata records `backend: docker`, `ptyMethod: docker-python-pty`, `exitCode: 0`, `ok: true`, and `stopReason: completed`.

However, `pibo debug session ps_room_move_fixture --json` shows the split state:

```json
{
  "session": {
    "id": "ps_room_move_fixture",
    "room_id": "room_old",
    "updated_at": "2026-08-30T00:02:00.000Z"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "chatRoomId": "room_new"
  },
  "room": {
    "sessionRoomId": "room_old"
  },
  "chat": {
    "pibo_session_id": "ps_room_move_fixture",
    "room_id": "room_old"
  }
}
```

A third migration run reports `skipped: 1`; the stale `room_id` remains because the target now has the same `updated_at` as the source.

## Control

Deleting only the disposable target `pibo.sqlite` after advancing the source, then importing that same `room_new` source into a fresh target, produces:

```json
{
  "room_id": "room_new",
  "metadata_room": "room_new",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-30T00:02:00.000Z"
}
```

This isolates the defect to the newer-row update path rather than legacy metadata parsing or initial insertion.

## Expected result

When a newer legacy row is accepted as an update, the migration should keep the target's structured room association and imported metadata coherent. If `metadata_json.chatRoomId` changes to `room_new`, `sessions.room_id` should also become `room_new` before the migration advances `updated_at` and reports the row as updated.

## Impact and severity

Suggested severity: moderate, migration-specific.

Re-running the documented idempotent migration against a changed legacy source can leave a session routed and listed under the old room while its imported metadata names the new room. The successful update count hides the partial update, and the copied timestamp prevents later reruns from repairing it.

records.title: Recursively index an existing package folder
records.body:
## User story

As a CaseGraph user, I want to index an existing package folder recursively so that CaseGraph can inventory its files, create reusable case-independent artifacts, and progressively enrich them without reorganizing or copying the source collection.

## Acceptance criteria

- The index operation starts from an explicitly selected folder or resolved package.
- The operation recursively inventories supported files and records relative path, media type, size, and SHA-256.
- Original source files remain unchanged.
- When the target package has opted into managed writes, CaseGraph can create validated sidecars and case-independent derived artifacts within that package.
- PDF extraction can create `ruling.md` and `ruling.md.casegraph.yaml` from `ruling.pdf` and `ruling.pdf.casegraph.yaml`.
- The derived-artifact sidecar records the exact source SHA-256 used for extraction.
- Unsupported files and extraction failures remain in the inventory with a clear status.
- Re-indexing unchanged content does not create duplicate artifact identities.
- A changed source SHA-256 is reported as a possible stale derivation.
- Automatic re-extraction, immutable source-version policy, and downstream reference reevaluation are deferred.
- Initial indexing does not present machine observations as verified case facts, legal propositions, or legal-effect relationships.

records.title: CallGraph.__build recurses without a visited set: RecursionError on recursive call graphs
records.body:
## Summary

`kirin.analysis.CallGraph` recurses into callees without tracking visited methods, so building a call graph for any method whose call graph contains a cycle raises `RecursionError`. This makes `CallGraph` unusable for the one task it is most obviously suited to: detecting recursion.

`kirin-toolchain` 0.22.11, `kirin/analysis/callgraph.py:32-42`:

```python
def __build(self, mt: ir.Method):
    for stmt in mt.callable_region.walk():
        if isinstance(stmt, func.Invoke):
            edges = self.edges.setdefault(stmt.callee, set())
            edges.add(mt)
            self.__build(stmt.callee)     # <-- no visited set
```

`self.edges` is populated as it goes, but is never consulted to decide whether to descend, so a self-referential or mutually-recursive method recurses until the Python stack is exhausted.

## Reproducer

```python
from bloqade import squin
from kirin.analysis.callgraph import CallGraph

@squin.kernel(fold=False)
def B(main):
    B(main)
    main()

CallGraph(B)   # RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

Confirmed on `kirin-toolchain` 0.22.11.

## Fix

Guard the descent on a visited set, e.g.:

```diff
-    def __build(self, mt: ir.Method):
+    def __build(self, mt: ir.Method, visited: set[ir.Method] | None = None):
+        visited = set() if visited is None else visited
+        if mt in visited:
+            return
+        visited.add(mt)
         for stmt in mt.callable_region.walk():
             if isinstance(stmt, func.Invoke):
                 edges = self.edges.setdefault(stmt.callee, set())
                 edges.add(mt)
-                self.__build(stmt.callee)
+                self.__build(stmt.callee, visited)
```

Cycles are then represented in `edges`/`backedges` (which is what a caller wanting to *detect* recursion needs) rather than blowing the stack.

Two notes on adjacent behaviour, in case they are also unintended:

- `edges` is documented as "caller -> callee" but is populated as `edges[callee].add(caller)` — i.e. it is keyed by callee. `get_neighbors`/`get_edges`/`get_nodes` all read it as though it were keyed by caller, so the direction is inverted relative to the docstring.
- Only `func.Invoke` is traversed; dynamic `func.Call` edges are invisible to the graph.

Found while looking for a way to reject recursive kernels in a downstream compiler (`bloqade-lanes`), where recursion currently causes an unbounded blowup in an abstract interpreter.

records.title: feat(di): DAG dependency resolution with precomputed parameter graph
records.body:
### Summary
In `src/dispatch.rs`, route dependencies are resolved linearly by feeding all previous dependency outputs 0..i-1 into `kwargs` of the subsequent dependency factory. This results in O(D^2) `PyDict::set_item` calls and prevents true directed acyclic graph (DAG) composition.

### Proposed Changes
1. Analyze dependency callables at registration/`freeze()` time and build a dependency DAG.
2. Perform topological sort and cycle validation at startup.
3. At request time, pass only the exact arguments required by each dependency callable.
4. Support concurrent resolution of independent async dependency nodes where applicable.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Circular dependencies are detected and rejected at startup/freeze time with a descriptive error.
- Dependencies only receive their declared keyword arguments.
- Existing linear dependency chains continue to work seamlessly.

records.title: [SST][P3] SST-P3-014: Add configurable call-graph precision
records.body:
## Problem

Higher-order IDE intelligence requires reusable graphs and flow facts with explicit soundness, completeness, and cost expectations. The missing platform outcome is advanced analysis services.

The roadmap identifies the concrete gap as **Add configurable call-graph precision**. Until it is delivered, the feature remains unavailable, incomplete at scale, or coupled to current Java and UI implementation details.

## Required outcome

Add configurable call-graph precision. The result must integrate with stable documents, locations, symbols, semantic snapshots, indexes, and workspace edits wherever applicable, while providing explicit lifecycle and failure semantics.

This issue defines the problem and acceptance boundary without supplying implementation code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add configurable call-graph precision.
- [ ] The capability remains language-extensible and handles source, generated, binary, decompiled, and virtual origins where relevant.
- [ ] Versioning, cancellation, concurrency, compatibility, security, performance, and bounded-resource behavior are defined as applicable.
- [ ] Automated tests cover cycles, recursion, aliasing, incomplete code, approximation, caching, invalidation, cancellation, and performance bounds.
- [ ] Existing Java behavior and Railroad's zero-error self-analysis baseline remain correct.
- [ ] Plugin-facing and user-facing behavior, limitations, approximation, and failure modes are documented.

## Dependencies and related work

- Roadmap group: **P3.3 Advanced analyses**
- Related SST umbrella: #63
- Roadmap reference: `SST-P3-014`

## Possible approach

Expose a narrow capability or query service with explicit snapshot inputs, cancellation, deterministic result semantics, and conformance tests for partial and failing providers.

Alternative implementations are welcome when they satisfy the same externally observable guarantees.
